question: to the Commission Nadine Morano (PPE), Céline Imart (PPE), Isabelle Le Callennec (PPE), Christophe Gomart (PPE), Tomáš Zdechovský (PPE), Andrey Kovatchev (PPE) Subject:

The EU laissez-passer is an additional travel document that facilitates, among other things, the procedures for obtaining visas for professional purposes. It is recognised by Member States’ authorities and may also be recognised by third countries under specific agreements. Its use is strictly limited to the exercise of official duties. In accordance with Protocol (No 7) on the Privileges and Immunities of the European Union and Regulation (EU) No 1417/2013, this document may be issued to Members of the European Parliament and to officials and other servants of the European Union. When MEPs do not have a diplomatic or service passport issued by their Member State, they can apply for a laissez-passer to facilitate their travel when they register for the exercise of their mandate. However, unlike officials, the function of Member of the European Parliament is not explicitly mentioned on page 4, which seems to run counter to the recognition of the official function of Member of the European Parliament. This situation appears all the more paradoxical given that Protocol (No 7) guarantees Members travel facilities equivalent to those granted to senior officials or representatives on official missions. Something therefore needs to be done to address this missing reference to the official function of Member of the European Parliament. When does the Commission intend to address this issue?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (31.8.2026) Article 6 of the Protocol on the privileges and immunities of the European Union (PPI) provides that ‘laissez-passer in a form to be prescribed by the Council, acting by a simple majority, [...] may be issued to members and servants of the institutions of the Union by the Presidents of those institutions’. Annex I to Council Regulation (EU) No 1417/2013 of 17 December 20131 laying down the form of the laissez-passer issued by the European Union requires that the ‘function’ be indicated on page 4 of the laissez-passer. However, no official list of functions to be indicated has been adopted, leaving this matter open to interpretation by each institution. Article 6 of the Protocol states that laissez-passer may be issued by the Presidents of each institution. Therefore, any request to indicate the official function of Member of the European Parliament on the laissez-passer must be addressed to the institution competent to issue them to Members of the European Parliament, namely the European Parliament.
